analysis:
Examined both excerpts and the complete change map for provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCache.swift. The only mapped change is eviction delegation at head lines 1772–1777 to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest. Its callback still constructs HMAC-tagged block paths and calls retireIndexedEntries; successful byte reclamation still increments eviction statistics. No concrete regression is established by these excerpts.
Unchanged head lines 511–650 enforce cache-salt-derived lookup, epoch/layout agreement, request-specific adoption tickets and per-entry reservation release. Head lines 430–477 stop background work and provide awaited teardown. Base lines 1863–1964 show fail-closed startup path checks and model/layout/block bindings; base lines 2050–2131 authenticate surviving blocks before durable-ready receipts. These behaviors relate chiefly to T-041, A-001, TB-007 and serving availability (A-018); the mapped change does not directly alter transport encryption, attestation, authorization or billing.
Integration must examine SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest and its result contract with retireIndexedEntries and SSDDiskBudget. The previous loop bounded attempts by an index snapshot, skipped undeletable victims, stopped on externalChange and returned indexedBytesFreed. The helper implementation is absent here, so preservation of those availability/accounting guarantees cannot be verified. This is a coverage question, not evidence of a missing control. No unrelated unchanged dependencies were reviewed.
